findings.title: The log row index is chunked into 200-row "pages" that buy nothing over a flat index array
findings.why: `MatchingPage`, `buildMatchingPages`, `pruneMatchingPages`, `appendMatchingIndices` and `getRowLogicalIndices` (~120 of the file's 259 lines, plus most of its 202-line test) exist only to keep the matching logical indices split into LOG_WINDOW_SIZE chunks. The upstream event buffer is capped at MAX_EVENTS = 5000 (libs/core/src/review/event-sequence.ts:65), so a single `readonly number[]` of matching indices plus a `firstRow` offset gives identical behaviour, makes window extraction one `slice` instead of a page scan, and removes the off-by-one edge cases in `pruneMatchingPages` (`firstRetainedOffset <= 0 && pageIndex === 0`).
findings.fix: Replace `matchingPages: readonly MatchingPage[]` with `matchingRows: readonly number[]` (logical indices) plus `firstRow: number`. `getEventRowBounds` becomes `{ start: firstRow, end: firstRow + matchingRows.length }`, `getRowLogicalIndices` becomes `matchingRows.slice(startRow - firstRow, endRow - firstRow)`, prune becomes one `findIndex` + `slice`, append becomes one spread. Delete `MatchingPage`, `buildMatchingPages`, `pruneMatchingPages`, `appendMatchingIndices` and the page-boundary cases in row-index.test.ts.
findings.note: Paging is real: ~120 of 259 lines plus page-boundary test cases exist only to chunk a matching-index list that libs/core/src/review/event-sequence.ts:65 caps at 5000 entries, and the only tested perf contract (row-index.test.ts:56 counts event property reads) is satisfied by incremental derivation, not by chunking — but the claim "buys nothing" overstates it (pages do give amortized O(1) append with structural sharing), so this is medium over-engineering, not high.

findings.title: `isMountedRef` plus its lifecycle effect are dead — the sibling ref check already covers unmount
findings.why: The unmount cleanup sets `activeReviewRequestRef.current = null`, and nothing can re-assign it after unmount (only `startReview` writes it, and that requires a mounted component). So `activeReviewRequestRef.current !== request` is already true on every post-unmount call and the `!isMountedRef.current` half of the condition can never be the deciding factor. A ref plus a mount effect that changes no behaviour is exactly the defensive noise a cold reader has to disprove.
findings.evidence: if (!isMountedRef.current || activeReviewRequestRef.current !== request) return false;
findings.fix: Delete `isMountedRef` (line 85), drop `isMountedRef.current = true/false` from the effect at lines 87-93 (keeping the `activeReviewRequestRef.current = null` cleanup, which is what actually guards the post-unmount `navigate`), and reduce the guard to `if (activeReviewRequestRef.current !== request) return false;`.
findings.note: Verified: startReview (presentation.tsx:121-128) is the only writer of activeReviewRequestRef and the unmount cleanup nulls it, so `!isMountedRef.current` can never be the deciding half of the guard — three lines of dead defensive state, but harmless.

findings.title: `useProviders` is a rename-only pass-through with a single consumer
findings.why: The hook adds no state, no memo, no error handling — it calls `mapProvidersWithStatus` and re-labels three functions from `useConfigActions`. Its only consumer is `use-provider-management.ts`, so the indirection just makes the reader open a second file to learn that `saveApiKey` is `saveCredentials`.
findings.evidence:
saveApiKey: saveCredentials,
    removeApiKey: deleteProviderCredentials,
    selectProvider: activateProvider,
findings.fix: Delete `use-providers.ts` and inline it into `useProviderManagement`: call `useConfigData()`/`useConfigActions()` there, derive `providers = mapProvidersWithStatus(providerStatus)`, and use the real names (`saveCredentials`, `deleteProviderCredentials`, `activateProvider`) at the call sites.
findings.note: use-providers.ts adds no state or logic and has exactly one consumer (use-provider-management.ts:23), so it only re-labels useConfigActions members; real but minor indirection, not medium.

findings.title: `useModelDialogFocusTrap` is not a focus trap; AGENTS.md reserves that term for libs/keys
findings.why: The hook owns zone state, a close-button ref and one ArrowDown binding — it never traps Tab or restores focus. AGENTS.md assigns "focus trap/restore" to `libs/keys`, so a cold reader looking for the dialog's trap lands here and finds a zone machine, while the real trapping lives in `Dialog`. The file's own JSDoc already contradicts its name ("Dialog focus-zone state plus the close-button boundary").
findings.fix: Rename the file to `use-dialog-zones.ts` and the export to `useModelDialogZones` (matching what the JSDoc already says), and update the two references in `use-dialog-keyboard.ts`.
findings.note: The hook owns only zone state, a close-button ref and one ArrowDown binding — no Tab trapping or focus restore — and its own JSDoc says "focus-zone state", so the name collides with the term AGENTS.md reserves for libs/keys; blast radius is two references, so low.

findings.title: `findFilterChip` exists but two other sites re-inline the same `findNavigationItemByValue` call verbatim
findings.why: Three sites resolve the same filter chip element. One goes through the named helper; the `useFocusZone` filters target (196-199) and `handleSeverityFilterBoundary` (296-300) paste the same three-property call instead. If the chip's navigation-item contract changes, two of the three break silently.

findings.title: Unreachable `default` branch kills exhaustiveness on a 6-arm switch of near-identical rows
findings.why: `OnboardingStep` is `(typeof WIZARD_STEPS)[number]` with exactly the six cases listed, so `default: return []` can never run — and it converts a future 7th step from a compile error into a silently empty footer. The six arms themselves differ only in two label strings each, which is copy-paste the type system could enforce.
findings.fix: Delete the `default` arm so TypeScript enforces exhaustiveness. Then collapse the six arms into one `Record<OnboardingStep, { navigate: string; select: string; enter: string }>` and build the four-row array once from it.
findings.note: OnboardingStep is (typeof WIZARD_STEPS)[number] with exactly the six cases listed (libs/core/src/onboarding/types.ts:11-19), so `default: return []` is unreachable and suppresses the TS2366 exhaustiveness error a seventh step would otherwise trigger.

findings.title: Two dead guards on values that are never falsy in the provider row
findings.why: `statusText` is a template literal, so it is always truthy and `{statusText && …}` never short-circuits. `subtitleText`'s `else` branch only runs when `provider.model` is truthy, so `|| undefined` is unreachable. Both read as "this can be empty", which is the opposite of the truth and costs the reader a re-derivation.
findings.evidence:
const statusText = `[ ${badge.label.toUpperCase()} ]`;
const subtitleText = !provider.model ? "Select model" : provider.model || undefined;
findings.fix: Render `<NavigationListStatus>{statusText}</NavigationListStatus>` unconditionally (line 185), and reduce line 173 to `const subtitleText = provider.model || "Select model";`.
findings.note: Both guards are genuinely dead — statusText is a bracketed template literal and the `|| undefined` sits in the branch where provider.model is already truthy — but they are two lines of noise, not a medium defect.

findings.title: Three wrappers over `getActionProps` diverge on whether they forward `actionProps.onFocus`, and one pays for it with shadow state
findings.why: `use-action-buttons.ts:85` forwards `actionProps.onFocus()`; this file and `api-key-dialog/use-keyboard.ts:131` drop it. Dropping it means the action row's own `focusedIndex` never learns about browser-driven (Tab/click) focus, which is why this file adds `tabFocusedFooterIndex` state, the `footerButtonIndex` reconciliation ternary (164-167) and an effect to clear it (330-332) — ~12 lines re-implementing what the dropped callback already does. Nothing marks the divergence as deliberate.
findings.fix: Forward `actionProps.onFocus()` alongside `setFocusZone("footer")` here and in `api-key-dialog/use-keyboard.ts:131`, then delete `tabFocusedFooterIndex`, the `footerButtonIndex` ternary and the effect at 330-332 (dialog.integration.test.tsx already covers Tab-into-footer highlighting). If any of the three must deviate, say why in one line.
findings.note: The divergence is real and undocumented (use-action-buttons.ts forwards actionProps.onFocus, this file and api-key-dialog/use-keyboard.ts do not, and this file compensates with tabFocusedFooterIndex plus a ternary and a clearing effect), but the proposed deletion is a behavioral change that no existing test in use-dialog-keyboard.footer.test.ts pins, so it needs verification rather than a blind fix — worth a one-line rationale at minimum.

findings.title: `selectedIssueId` and `highlightedIssueId` are the same value under two names
findings.why: Both keys return `effectiveSelectedId`. `use-results-keyboard.ts` then threads them to `IssueListPane` as two separate props and to `useScopedNavigation` as `highlighted`, so a reader reasonably assumes selection and highlight can diverge (they cannot) and writes code defending against a state that never occurs.

selectedIssueId: effectiveSelectedId,
    setSelectedIssueId,
    highlightedIssueId: effectiveSelectedId,
findings.fix: Return one `selectedIssueId` and let `use-results-keyboard.ts` pass it to both the `highlighted` and `selectedId` props at the call sites, so the single-value fact is visible where it matters. Add a one-line note there if the pane's two props are intentionally kept separate for future divergence.

findings.title: Two stacked single-use prop-forwarding wrappers around one `RadioGroup`
findings.why: `ModelStep` renders `ModelInfoList` (one call site) which renders `ModelRadioGroup` (one call site) which renders `RadioGroup`. Both wrappers declare `Omit<ModelStepProps, "provider">`-derived prop types and forward six props unchanged; `ModelRadioGroup` adds only `highlighted` state and two two-line handlers. Reading how a model gets selected takes three hops through the same file.
findings.fix: Merge `ModelRadioGroup` into `ModelInfoList`: keep the `highlighted` state and `handleChange`/`handleEnter` there and render `RadioGroup` directly with the `RadioGroupItem` children. Delete `ModelRadioGroupProps`.
findings.note: Verified three single-call-site hops in one file (ModelStep -> ModelInfoList -> ModelRadioGroup) with six props forwarded unchanged and an Omit-derived prop type per layer; merging the inner two is safe and mechanical, so this is a low-grade layering nit.

findings.title: Redundant second lookup and guard after a successful `findIndex`
findings.why: When `index !== -1`, `PROVIDER_FILTER_LABELS[index]` is guaranteed defined and its `.value` is the `value` that was just matched, so the `?.` and the `if (!nextFilter) return` can never fire. The reader has to prove that before moving on.
findings.evidence:
const nextFilter = PROVIDER_FILTER_LABELS[index]?.value;
            if (!nextFilter) return;
findings.fix: Replace the `findIndex` + re-lookup with `const index = PROVIDER_FILTER_LABELS.findIndex((item) => item.value === value); if (index === -1) return;` then use `value` directly for `onFilterChange`, dropping both redundant lines.
findings.note: The re-lookup and `if (!nextFilter) return` are runtime-dead after a successful findIndex, but note the proposed fix is wrong as written: ToggleGroup's onChange yields ProviderFilter | null, so dropping the lookup requires an explicit `if (value === null) return;` to satisfy the type (noUncheckedIndexedAccess is on in libs/core/tsconfig/base.json:18).

findings.title: `handleRunsBoundary`'s "down" branch is unreachable — the caller already filters to "previous"
findings.why: `page.tsx:265-269` only calls it when `direction === "previous"`, then converts it through `toVerticalBoundaryDirection`, which maps `"previous"` to `"up"` unconditionally. So the `direction` parameter has exactly one possible value and the implicit "down" no-op is dead. Two guards for one decision.
findings.fix: Drop the parameter: `const handleRunsBoundary = () => setFocusZone("search");` and simplify the call site to `if (direction === "previous") handleRunsBoundary();`, removing the `toVerticalBoundaryDirection` import if it becomes unused there.
findings.note: Confirmed dead branch: the sole call site (page.tsx:265-269) fires only for "previous", and the single-arg toVerticalBoundaryDirection overload maps "previous" to "up" unconditionally (libs/keys/src/core/navigation-directions.ts:34), so handleRunsBoundary's parameter has one possible value.

findings.title: `activeRunId` is a bare alias for `selectedRunId`
findings.why: The alias introduces a second vocabulary for one value inside a component that also uses `selectedRunId` directly (lines 260, 263-264, 350), so the reader has to check whether "active" and "selected" mean different things. They do not.

findings.title: Single-use one-line wrapper around `pluralize`

findings.title: Raw `false`/`true` returns where `libs/keys` exports the named `DECLINE` sentinel

findings.title: IIFE for a decision the sibling settings hub already expresses as a named function

Here the same rule is an inline IIFE inside the component body, so the two surfaces read differently for one behaviour.

Provider status load: …

` assertion in `use-config.test.tsx:71`. Re-add only when a screen actually needs provider-status load state.

findings.title: Guard test mocks and asserts on `api.checkConfig`, which the guards never call

The mock, three `mockCheckConfig.mockResolvedValue(...)` setups and two `expect(mockCheckConfig).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` assertions test a mock, and the test title invents a "legacy check" concept that exists nowhere in the codebase.

findings.title: Dead SSR guards in a client-only SPA
findings.why: `apps/web` has no SSR entry (only `ReactDOM.createRoot` in `main.tsx`, vite build, jsdom tests), so `typeof window === "undefined"` is never true and the `getServerSnapshot` argument is never invoked. The file already proves the assumption by calling `window.matchMedia` unguarded on line 16.

findings.title: `getDefaultApiUrl`/`getShutdownToken` branch on a no-window case that cannot happen

findings.title: Four-level single-consumer wrapper chain around one error boundary
findings.why: `__root.tsx` → `RouteOutletBoundary` → `LocationAwareRouteErrorBoundary` → `RouteErrorBoundary` — each layer has exactly one production consumer and adds one line (a flex div, a `key`, the class). Tracing "what catches a route render error" requires four hops through two files.

findings.title: Three parallel `Record<HeaderServerState, …>` maps for one concept
findings.why: `SERVER_STATE_WORD`, `SERVER_DOT_STATUS` and `SERVER_ARIA_WORD` are keyed identically and always read together for the same state; adding a fourth transport state means editing three separate literals and hoping none is missed. The file's own `LAYOUT` constant already demonstrates the one-record-many-slots shape (with a comment defending it).

findings.title: `FocusElement` is a generic-sounding shared type that is really the API-key form's focus targets
findings.why: The name and its home in the app-wide `types/` folder suggest a DOM/focus primitive; the members (`paste`/`input`/`env`/`cancel`/`confirm`) are the five focus stops of the API-key entry form and nothing else uses it. AGENTS.md requires names that describe the semantic thing, and this one misdirects every reader of `api-key-method-selector.tsx`.

findings.fix: Rename the type to `ApiKeyFocusTarget` and the file to `types/api-key-focus-target.ts`, updating the three consumers (`components/shared/api-key-method-selector.tsx`, `features/onboarding/components/steps/api-key-step.tsx`, `features/providers/components/api-key-dialog/use-keyboard.ts`) and the test.

findings.title: Imperative `document.title` write with no explanation while every route uses `head`
findings.why: Every route in `router.tsx` sets its title declaratively via `head: () => ({ meta: [{ title: … }] })`. This one page does it in an effect with a save/restore dance and a `document.title === notFoundTitle` guard, and nothing states the constraint (a not-found render has no matched route, so `HeadContent` never emits a title). Thirty seconds of reading does not explain it.
findings.fix: Add one sentence above the effect: "No route matches a not-found render, so `head()`/`HeadContent` never fires here; the title is set (and restored on unmount, unless another screen already changed it) by hand."
findings.note: Verified the constraint is real (the root route declares no head(), so a defaultNotFoundComponent render never emits a title through HeadContent) and unstated, and this repo consistently documents non-obvious decisions; a one-line comment, so low.

findings.title: Two independent dialog-suppression mechanisms with nothing saying why both are needed
findings.why: `enabled` suppresses shortcuts when the active keys scope looks like a dialog, and every handler additionally calls `hasOpenDialog()`. Both are actually required — the api-key dialog registers `useScope("api-key-dialog")` while the model-select dialog registers no scope at all — but a reader sees a belt-and-braces duplicate and will delete one.
findings.fix: Add one sentence above `hasOpenDialog`: "Not every dialog registers a keys scope (the model-select dialog does not), so the open `<dialog>` in the DOM is the second, authoritative check."
findings.note: Verified both halves are load-bearing: api-key-dialog/use-keyboard.ts:91 registers useScope("api-key-dialog") while model-select-dialog registers no scope at all (only useScopedNavigation), so hasOpenDialog() is the only thing suppressing shortcuts there — non-obvious redundancy worth one sentence, low.

findings.title: Node builtins loaded through string-variable indirection with no stated reason
findings.why: `const fsSpecifier = "node:fs"` followed by `import(fsSpecifier)` is deliberate evasion of static import analysis, and `declare const process` at line 9 hand-rolls a global the tsconfig does not provide. Both read as workarounds a reader cannot reconstruct, and either will be "simplified" back into a top-level `import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"` that then breaks the run.

findings.title: React test written in `.ts`, forcing `createElement` noise, with two near-identical builders
findings.why: Every other component test in the surface is `.tsx` and uses JSX; here the extension forces `createElement(FooterProvider, null, createElement(...))` at three call sites, and `renderPageFooter` re-builds by hand exactly what `createPageFooterElement` already returns.

findings.note: Confirmed: the file is .ts among .tsx component tests, forcing three createElement calls, and renderPageFooter hand-rebuilds exactly what createPageFooterElement returns two lines below it — trivial but real duplication, low.

findings.title: Prop/helper types exported but never imported anywhere
findings.why: `apps/web` is an application, not a package: exporting types nothing imports widens the apparent API and invites the next reader to assume there is an external consumer. Confirmed unused across the repo: `SeverityBarProps`, `SeverityBreakdownProps`, `SeverityConfig`, `CardLayoutProps`, `FailureAction`, `StorageSelectorContentProps`, `TrustPanelProps`, `SetState`, `TrustFormFocusZone`.
findings.fix: Drop the `export` keyword from these type declarations (keep `FailureViewProps`, which `failure-view.test.tsx` imports, and `HeaderServerState`/`TrustPermissionsContentProps`/`TrustFormAction`, which cross files).
findings.note: Spot-checked all nine names repo-wide: each is referenced only inside its own file (the cli/diffgazer SeverityBreakdownProps/TrustPanelProps hits are separate local declarations), and the finding correctly exempts FailureViewProps and HeaderServerState, which do cross files.

findings.title: `EMPTY_FOOTER_SHORTCUTS: []` — neither the empty-tuple type nor the hoisting is explained

findings.title: 264-line stdin escape-sequence parser + stdin Proxy with zero statement of the problem it solves
findings.why: This is the single hardest file in the TUI shell to read cold. Nothing anywhere says what `legacy-modified` means, why an ESC byte is withheld for 50ms, or why `stdin` is wrapped in a Proxy at all. A reader cannot tell whether this is essential or accidental, and the consumer (`app/providers/keyboard.tsx:57`) is equally silent.
findings.fix: Add a 3-4 line file header stating the constraint the code cannot show: terminals encode Alt+<key> as ESC followed by the key ("legacy modified" encoding), Ink cannot distinguish that from a bare Escape, so a lone ESC is held for ESCAPE_PREFIX_HOLD_MS before being released, and the Proxy exists to intercept `read()` without replacing the real stdin Ink needs. Add one sentence at app/providers/keyboard.tsx:57 stating that `consume()` must be called exactly once per Ink input event to stay in lockstep with the queue.
findings.note: Verified: 264 lines with zero comments, and the auditor's reading is correct (parseEscape classifies ESC+printable as Alt, the Proxy only overrides read() and binds the rest to the real stdin, the 50ms hold disambiguates bare Escape) — but the test file names the mechanism fairly well ("rejects legacy Alt+S ... before Ink drops raw input details", "expires a true bare Escape"), so a missing file header is medium, not high.

findings.title: ScrollArea's content-measurement state machine (isMeasuringContent / contentReference) is unexplained anywhere

This is the exact class of code the reviewer will stop on.
findings.fix: Add one comment above line 90 stating the constraint: static children have no known row count until `useBoxMetrics` reports one, so on a content swap the box must render unclamped for one commit (`minHeight: undefined`) to be measured, then re-clamp to the measured `rowCount` — `isMeasuringContent` is that one-commit window.
findings.note: Verified at scroll-area.tsx:93-96 and 193: the two-pass measure (minHeight undefined for one commit, re-clamp once measuredStaticRowCount === scrollState.rowCount) is real and undocumented, but the component has 19 behavior tests covering it, so a missing comment is medium rather than high.

findings.note: rg confirms listReviews is referenced only by reviews.test.ts and app-review-rekey.test.ts and listFromIndex only by listReviews, while the live route (router/history.ts:29) uses listReviewPage — ~75 lines of unreachable parallel listing logic, but dead code, not a release blocker.

findings.title: `createCollection` is a generic multi-collection factory with exactly one collection, and half its surface is never called in production
findings.why: The only production instantiation is `reviewStore`. `collection.list()`, `collection.readMetadata()` and external `ensureDir()` are referenced only from `persistence.test.ts` — and `getMetadata`/`metadataSchema`/`extractMetadataFromFile` exist solely to serve those. That is ~85 lines of generic plumbing (plus `Collection`/`CollectionConfig` in types.ts) whose only consumer is its own test file.
findings.fix: Delete `list`, `readMetadata`, `extractMetadataFromFile`, the `getMetadata`/`metadataSchema` config fields and the corresponding tests. Then collapse the remaining `read`/`readDetailed`/`write`/`ensureDir` into a concrete `reviewStore` module (no `<T, M, D>` generics) since there is one collection.
findings.note: Confirmed list()/readMetadata()/extractMetadataFromFile plus the metadataSchema/getMetadata/coerceMetadata config fields have no production reader (reviews.ts uses only readDetailed/read/write via readReviewMetadata), though the prescription to strip all generics from a still-reasonable factory goes beyond the evidence.

findings.title: Five persistence write paths are test-only, and three of them bypass the cross-process file lock the production paths depend on
findings.why: `persistConfig`, `persistConfigMergedAsync` (config.ts), `persistSecrets`, `removeSecretsFile` (secrets.ts) and `persistTrust` (trust.ts) are referenced only from `persistence-*.test.ts`. The sync ones write with `writeJsonFileSync` outside `withFileTransactionLock`, so they are live footguns: anyone reaching for the obvious-looking `persistConfig` silently breaks the locking invariant the async path enforces.
findings.fix: Delete `persistConfig`, `persistConfigMergedAsync`, `persistSecrets`, `removeSecretsFile` and `persistTrust`; retarget their tests at the locked paths (`withConfigFileTransaction`, `persistSecretsAsync`, `persistTrustRecordAsync`) which are what production actually runs.
findings.note: persistConfig (persistence/config.ts:184), persistConfigMergedAsync, persistSecrets, removeSecretsFile and persistTrust have zero non-test references repo-wide, and the three sync ones do write via writeJsonFileSync outside withFileTransactionLock as claimed.

findings.title: `store.ts` is a 1088-line module that also owns the entire secrets recovery-WAL subsystem
findings.why: Besides the config store itself, the file holds the recovery-record schema, serialize/restore, startup reconcile, begin/clear recovery, and the multi-way keyring+config+secrets rollback ladders. Reading `saveProviderCredentials` requires holding six separate rollback concepts in your head at once. The file's own comment justifies keeping config+secrets *state* inline — it does not justify the WAL living here.
findings.fix: Move the recovery-record concern into `shared/lib/config/secrets-recovery.ts`: `SecretsRecoveryRecordSchema`, `getSecretsRecoveryPath`, `serializeSecretsState`, `restoreRecoveryRecordSync`, `readSecretsRecovery`, `reconcileSecretsRecoveryAtStartup` and `rollbackFailure` are all closure-free top-level functions and move without touching `createConfigStore`'s internals.
findings.note: store.ts is 1088 lines and the recovery-WAL block (SecretsRecoveryRecordSchema through reconcileSecretsRecoveryAtStartup, lines 84-170) is top-level and closure-free; the file's own comment at line 223 justifies only the config+secrets state being inline, not the WAL.

findings.title: `partialOnAllFailed` is an extensibility flag whose only caller always passes `false`, making its whole branch unreachable
findings.why: `orchestrateReview` has exactly one production call site (`pipeline.ts:131`, `partialOnAllFailed: false`). The `ok({ issues: [], ... })` branch and the option's documented two-mode contract in `engine/types.ts` describe behavior that cannot occur.
findings.fix: Delete `partialOnAllFailed` from `OrchestrationOptions` and the branch at 233-243, leaving `if (allLensesFailed && lastError !== null) return err(lastError);`.
findings.note: partialOnAllFailed is passed false at the only production call site (pipeline.ts:134) and true only in orchestrate.test.ts, so the ok-partial branch is production-unreachable — a genuine but small YAGNI flag.

findings.title: Lens/filter resolution is done twice — orchestrate's `profile` fallbacks and `["correctness"]` default are unreachable
findings.why: `pipeline.executeReview` already resolved lenses and filter via `resolveReviewDefaults` and passes only `{ lenses, filter }`. `reviewOptions.profile` is never set by any caller, so both `profile?.lenses` and `profile?.filter` branches are dead, and the hardcoded `["correctness"]` default duplicates a decision `resolveActiveLenses` already made.
findings.fix: Change the signature to require the already-resolved `{ lenses: LensId[]; filter?: SeverityFilter }` and delete the profile fallbacks, the `[...new Set(...)]` re-dedupe and the `["correctness"]` default — `resolveReviewDefaults` owns all three.

findings.title: `failedLenses` and `droppedIncompleteProviderIssues` are computed and returned in `OrchestrationOutcome` but never read
findings.why: `pipeline.executeReview` maps only `issues`, `lensStats`, `droppedDuplicates`, `droppedBelowThreshold` and `minSeverity` into `ReviewOutcome`. `failedLenses` exists only so `failedLenses.length` can be compared for `allLensesFailed`; its `errorCode`/`errorMessage` payload is built at both push sites and thrown away.
findings.fix: Replace the `failedLenses` array with a `failedLensCount` counter, drop it and `droppedIncompleteProviderIssues` from `OrchestrationOutcome` (the latter is already carried where it matters, in the `orchestrator_complete` event).
findings.note: pipeline.ts:152-157 maps only issues/lensStats/droppedDuplicates/droppedBelowThreshold/minSeverity, so failedLenses' errorCode/errorMessage payload and the outcome-level droppedIncompleteProviderIssues are written and never read — real but minor unread return data.

findings.title: `WorkspaceRoot.includeSelf` / `includeChildren` are config knobs with a single constant value, leaving two dead branches
findings.why: `FALLBACK_WORKSPACE_ROOTS` is the only value ever passed, and both entries are `{ includeSelf: false, includeChildren: true }`. So `if (root.includeSelf)` never runs and `if (!root.includeChildren) continue;` never triggers — configuration for a variation that does not exist.
findings.fix: Drop both flags from `WorkspaceRoot` and delete the `includeSelf` block (215-217) and the `includeChildren` guard (218); the fallback scan is unconditionally "children of apps/ and packages/".
findings.note: FALLBACK_WORKSPACE_ROOTS is the only WorkspaceRoot[] ever constructed and both entries are includeSelf:false/includeChildren:true, so discovery.ts:215-218 has one never-taken branch and one never-triggered guard; small YAGNI, not medium.

findings.title: The same zod-issue formatter is written three times, one of them inline
findings.why: Identical `issue.path.length > 0 ? issue.path.join(".") : "<root>"` + `"; "` join logic appears in `manifest.ts:17` (exported and imported by discovery.ts), `shared/lib/config/persistence/load-json.ts:7`, and inline in `features/review/context/snapshot/artifacts.ts:111`. Three occurrences is the extraction threshold, and it currently lives in a module named for reading package manifests.
findings.fix: Move it once to `shared/lib/errors.ts` (or a new `shared/lib/zod-issues.ts`) and import it from all three sites; remove the copy in `load-json.ts` and the inline block in `artifacts.ts`.
findings.note: Byte-identical path.join(".")/'<root>'/'; ' formatter verified at manifest.ts:17, load-json.ts:7 and inline at artifacts.ts:111-116; real triple duplication but a pure log-formatting helper with no behavioral blast radius.

findings.title: A 110-line test fixture lives in the production `shared/lib/ai/` directory and ships in the bundle
findings.why: `MODELS_DEV_SAMPLE` is imported only by `models-dev-catalog-fetch.test.ts` and `models-dev-catalog-resolution.test.ts`. `cli/server` already has `shared/lib/testing/` for exactly this (`factories.ts`, `http.ts`), and `cli/server` is bundled into the `diffgazer` binary via tsup `noExternal`, so the fixture rides along.

// cli/server-local copy so server tests do not import a libs/core test fixture.

export const MODELS_DEV_SAMPLE: unknown = {

findings.title: A git error is classified into a typed code, the code is discarded, then re-derived by string-prefix matching on the message
findings.why: `createGitDiffError` runs `classifyError` to produce a `GitDiffErrorCode`, then throws the code away by returning a bare `Error`. `getReviewErrorCodeForGitDiff` recovers it with `startsWith("Git is not installed")` — so editing that user-facing copy in `git/errors.ts:17` silently downgrades GIT_NOT_FOUND to GENERATION_FAILED with no test or type failing.
findings.fix: Have `createGitDiffError` return `{ code: GitDiffErrorCode; message: string }` instead of an `Error`, and map `code === "GIT_NOT_FOUND"` directly in `diff.ts`.
findings.note: createGitDiffError does classify into GitDiffErrorCode then return a bare Error, and diff.ts:17 recovers GIT_NOT_FOUND via startsWith on the user-facing copy defined at git/errors.ts:17 — editing that string silently changes the wire error code with nothing failing.

findings.title: `ObservedDirectoryLock` re-declares the `kind: "directory"` member of `ObservedLock` field-for-field
findings.why: Two structural declarations of the same shape 6 lines apart that must be kept in sync by hand; adding a field to the union member and forgetting the interface (or vice versa) silently splits the type.
findings.fix: Replace the interface with `type ObservedDirectoryLock = Extract<ObservedLock, { kind: "directory" }>;`.
findings.note: ObservedDirectoryLock (file-lock.ts:45-50) restates the ObservedLock 'directory' member field-for-field six lines below it; the Extract<> fix is exact but the risk is confined to one file.

findings.title: The 415 handler hand-rolls the error envelope because 415 is missing from the `ErrorStatus` allowlist
findings.why: Every other error in the server goes through `errorResponse`, which is typed against the closed `WireErrorCode`/`ErrorStatus` vocabulary precisely so an envelope can't drift. This one route bypasses that and constructs `{ error: { message, code } }` by hand — the exact drift the typed helper exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Add `415: 415` to `VALID_ERROR_STATUSES` in `shared/lib/http/response.ts` and call `errorResponse(c, "Content-Type must be application/json", ErrorCode.VALIDATION_ERROR, 415)`.
findings.note: 415 is absent from VALID_ERROR_STATUSES so sessions.ts:40-47 hand-builds the envelope the documented closed WireErrorCode/ErrorStatus contract exists to enforce; the shape happens to match today, making this consistency rather than correctness.

findings.title: Two pure re-export lines with zero consumers
findings.why: `persistence.ts:142` re-exports `Collection`/`StoreError`/`StoreErrorCode` from `./types.js`, but the only importer of `persistence.js` (`reviews.ts:25`) imports `createCollection` alone and takes the types straight from `./types.js`. The same pattern sits at `shared/lib/git/errors.ts:5` re-exporting `GitDiffErrorCode`, which nobody imports from `errors.js`.
findings.evidence: export type { Collection, StoreError, StoreErrorCode } from "./types.js";
findings.fix: Delete both re-export lines. Consumers already import from the owning `types.js` modules.
findings.note: Verified persistence.js's only importer (reviews.ts:25) takes just createCollection and pulls types from ./types.js, and nothing imports GitDiffErrorCode from git/errors.js — both re-export lines are unreferenced.

findings.title: `ensureIssueEvidence` and `MAX_SYNTHESIZED_EVIDENCE_JSON_BYTES_PER_REVIEW` exist only for their own tests
findings.why: Production calls `createIssueEvidenceResolver(diff)` directly (`analysis.ts:211`); `ensureIssueEvidence` is a one-line forwarder used only by `evidence.test.ts`. `MAX_SYNTHESIZED_EVIDENCE_JSON_BYTES_PER_REVIEW` is a derived constant whose only reference is an assertion in `issues-envelope.test.ts` that re-derives the same multiplication.

findings.note: ensureIssueEvidence is a one-line forwarder used only by evidence.test.ts while analysis.ts:211 calls createIssueEvidenceResolver directly; the constant is weaker evidence since issues-envelope.test.ts:146 uses it to assert two derivations agree.

findings.title: `isValidUuid` is defined twice, identically, in sibling files in the same directory
findings.why: `project-index.ts:18` exports it (and `reviews.ts:33` imports it from there), while `persistence.ts:31` keeps a private byte-identical copy. Two definitions of one predicate three files apart invites them to diverge.

findings.fix: Delete the copy in `persistence.ts` and import the exported one from `./project-index.js` (or move it to a shared spot if the import direction is undesirable).
findings.note: project-index.ts:18 exports isValidUuid (imported by reviews.ts:33) and persistence.ts:31 keeps a byte-identical private copy in the same directory — a true duplicate, but a one-line predicate.

findings.title: `createPromptFileIdentities` is exported but used only inside its own file
findings.why: The only reference outside its declaration is line 187 in `buildReviewPrompt`. An exported symbol reads as part of the module contract and makes readers hunt for external consumers that do not exist.
findings.fix: Drop the `export` keyword (or inline the one-line `.map` into `buildReviewPrompt`).
findings.note: createPromptFileIdentities has exactly one reference, prompts.ts:187 inside the same module, and not even a test importer, so the export widens the module contract for nothing.

findings.title: `withSnapshotLock` is a pass-through wrapper around a lock that is itself used once
findings.why: `createKeyedLock` → `lockSnapshot` → `withSnapshotLock` → `buildSnapshot` is three names for one call. `withSnapshotLock` has exactly one call site, three lines below its definition, and adds no logic.

findings.note: withSnapshotLock (build.ts:12-14) adds no logic over lockSnapshot and has one call site three lines below, while the other createKeyedLock consumers (review-lock.ts, project-index.ts) call their lock directly.

findings.title: `prepareAggregateRead()`'s Result is silently discarded in three getters but propagated in a fourth
findings.why: `getSettings`, `getProviders` and `getActiveProvider` call it as a bare statement and serve possibly-stale state on a recovery error, while `getProviderApiKey` returns the error. A reader cannot tell whether the dropped Result is a deliberate read-only concession or an oversight, and nothing in the code says.
findings.fix: Add one sentence above the three getters stating that read-only getters intentionally serve the WAL snapshot on a recovery error because `ConfigStore` gives them no error channel — or make them return `Result` like `getProviderApiKey`.
findings.note: getSettings/getProviders/getActiveProvider call prepareAggregateRead() as a bare statement while getProviderApiKey (store.ts:788) propagates its Result, and nothing states whether serving the stale WAL snapshot is deliberate.

findings.title: `ProviderModelsResult` is an alias for `ProviderModelsResponse` that adds no meaning
findings.why: A second name for the same core type means readers must check whether the two ever diverge, and `getProviderModels` returns the alias while `features/config/service.ts` consumes it as `ProviderModelsResponse`.
findings.evidence:
export type ProviderModelsResult = ProviderModelsResponse;

type ResultSource = ProviderModelsResult["source"];
findings.fix: Delete the alias and use `ProviderModelsResponse` throughout this file (`ResultSource` becomes `ProviderModelsResponse["source"]`).

findings.title: `requireRepoAccess` reads the project trust twice per request for two checks that overlap
findings.why: It calls `getStore().getProjectInfo(projectRoot)` itself, then calls `hasRepoReadAccess(projectRoot)` which performs the identical lookup again. The first condition (`!trust?.capabilities.readFiles`) is also a strict subset of what `hasRepoReadAccess` checks, so the flow reads as two guards where there is one decision with two messages.

const { trust } = getStore().getProjectInfo(projectRoot);

  if (!trust?.capabilities.readFiles) {
findings.fix: Read `trust` once and branch on it locally: `if (!trust?.capabilities.readFiles) return <not granted>; if (trust.repoRoot !== projectRoot) return <wrong root>;` — dropping the second store read and the `hasRepoReadAccess` call from this path.

findings.title: Cascade-orphan / blocked-dependent removal logic has no test file at all
findings.why: AGENTS.md names this exact behavior a contract ("`dgadd remove` must respect ownership metadata and must not remove copied shared dependencies still needed by retained installed items"), yet `expandRemoval`/`dependentsOf` — a fixpoint loop plus a keys-vs-ui dependent scan — is the only remove module with no test. The `blocked` path is tested only in libs/registry with an injected stub `expandRequestedNames`, so the real implementation's cascade and block decisions are unverified.
findings.fix: Add `cli/add/src/commands/remove/dependencies.test.ts` covering: (a) a transitive whose only dependent is also being removed cascades out, (b) a transitive still needed by a retained item is not cascaded, (c) an explicitly requested item with retained dependents lands in `blocked` and is dropped from `toRemove`, (d) a copy-mode `keys/*` hook is treated as a dependency of its `ui/*` owner but a package-mode one is not, (e) the `manifestAbsent` branch still returns the requested names.

findings.title: The `@diffgazer/keys` registry-dependency prefix pair is redefined in three places inside this scope (and more outside)
findings.why: The same two-element prefix list is the parsing contract for every keys registry dependency. It is declared twice as a private const and open-coded a third time as inline string literals, in different orders. Adding or renaming a namespace prefix silently fixes one code path and breaks the others.
findings.fix: Export a single `KEYS_REGISTRY_DEPENDENCY_PREFIXES` (and a `parseKeysDependencyRef` helper) from `@diffgazer/registry/schemas`, then have `dist-keys.ts`, `cli/add/src/commands/add/integration.ts`, and `cli/add/src/utils/keys-copy-bundle.ts` import it. `libs/ui/scripts/registry/fs.ts` and `libs/ui/scripts/build-docs-data.ts` carry the same const and should follow.
findings.note: Verified the prefix pair is re-declared in dist-keys.ts:3, cli/add/src/commands/add/integration.ts:13, libs/ui/scripts/registry/fs.ts:11 and build-docs-data.ts:28 (in two different orders) and open-coded again in keys-copy-bundle.ts:102-106 and rewrite-keys-imports.ts:49,159; both consuming packages already depend on @diffgazer/registry so consolidation is free — but it is a two-string constant with no demonstrable failure, so high is overcalibrated.

findings.title: Command factories re-declare their workflow's options interface and forward it field-by-field
findings.why: `RemoveCommandConfig` is exactly `Omit<RunRemoveWorkflowOptions, "cwd"|"names"|"yes"|"dryRun"|"force">` — 15 members typed twice — and `buildRemoveAction` then copies all 15 across by hand. `DiffCommandConfig`/`buildDiffAction` is the same pattern. Adding one workflow option means editing three places, and a forgotten line in the forwarding block silently drops a caller's callback with no type error.
findings.fix: Define `export type RemoveCommandConfig<TItem, TConfig> = Omit<RunRemoveWorkflowOptions<TItem, TConfig>, "cwd" | "names" | "yes" | "dryRun" | "force">` and call `runRemoveWorkflow({ ...config, cwd, names, yes: opts.yes ?? false, dryRun: opts.dryRun ?? false, force: opts.force ?? false })`. Apply the same to `command-factories/diff.ts` (`Omit<RunDiffWorkflowOptions, "cwd" | "requestedNames" | "renderChangedFile">`).
findings.note: RemoveCommandConfig restates 15 members of RunRemoveWorkflowOptions verbatim and buildRemoveAction forwards each by hand (diff.ts does the same for 7); since canRemoveFile, resolveTransactionFiles, findOrphanedDeps, expandRequestedNames and onAfterRemove are all optional, dropping a forwarding line would silently disable a caller's callback with no type error — real, but a mechanical refactor, not high.

findings.title: `planIntegrationModeMigration` builds six interlocking sets with no statement of what the plan means
findings.why: 82 lines produce `retainedCopyHooks`, `explicitHooks`, `candidateHooks`, `retainedHooks`, `retainedFilePaths`, `removeManifestNames`, and `filesToRemove` with no doc comment; the reader cannot tell from the code why a hook that is both a candidate and explicit must survive, or why `requestedMode === "copy"` flips the retained set. Every other non-obvious block in this package carries an explaining comment — this, the most intricate one, does not.
findings.fix: Add a 2-3 line comment above the function stating the invariant it enforces — roughly: "a copied hook file is deleted only when no retained ui/* item still installs it in copy mode AND no keys/* item was installed explicitly; everything else stays on disk" — and name the two phases with local helpers (`collectRetainedHooks`, `collectRemovableHooks`) so the set algebra is readable.
findings.note: planIntegrationModeMigration really does build retainedCopyHooks/explicitHooks/candidateHooks/retainedHooks/retainedFilePaths/removeManifestNames/filesToRemove across ~70 lines with no doc comment while the rest of the package (css.ts, transaction paths) explains every non-obvious block — a documentation gap, not a defect, so medium is too high.

findings.title: `renderChangedFile` is an injection point whose only value is a function defined in the same file
findings.why: `runDiffWorkflow` is called from exactly one place (`command-factories/diff.ts:30`), which always passes `renderDiffPatch` — exported from `workflows/diff.ts` itself. The parameter is threaded through `RunDiffWorkflowOptions`, `diffFile`'s signature, and a `Pick<...>` type just to reach the function next to it.
findings.fix: Delete `renderChangedFile` from `RunDiffWorkflowOptions`, drop the second parameter of `diffFile`, call `renderDiffPatch` directly at `workflows/diff.ts:95`, and remove `renderChangedFile: renderDiffPatch` from `command-factories/diff.ts`.
findings.note: Verified renderChangedFile has exactly one producer (renderDiffPatch, exported from workflows/diff.ts itself) and one consumer (command-factories/diff.ts:30), with no test injecting an alternative, so the seam is threaded through three type declarations to reach the function next to it.

findings.title: `createItemAccessors(...).validate` and its `validateItems` helper are never called
findings.why: `createItemAccessors` has exactly one consumer (`cli/add/src/context.ts:232`), which uses only `requireConfig` and `getOrThrow`. `validate`/`validateItems` — 13 lines plus a bespoke error message — are unreachable, and their message format has silently diverged from the one `getItemOrThrow` emits.

findings.note: Confirmed dead: ctx.items is only ever used for requireConfig and getOrThrow (list.ts, remove.ts, add/command.ts, file-ops.ts, css-chunks.ts, namespaces.ts), so validate/validateItems are unreachable — but it is 13 lines of a private workspace package, so low rather than medium.

findings.title: `rewriteRelativeJsExtensionsForCopy` is a rename-only wrapper around `stripRelativeJsExtensions`
findings.why: The function body is a single forwarding call with no added logic, and both call sites are in the same package. It buys an extra module hop and a second name for one behavior, so a reader chasing the copy-mode transform has to open two files to learn nothing.
findings.fix: Delete the wrapper and import `stripRelativeJsExtensions` from `@diffgazer/registry` directly in `cli/add/src/commands/add/file-ops.ts:66` and `cli/add/src/utils/registry.ts:66`.

findings.title: A throwing assertion is wrapped in try/catch twice to serve as a boolean zod refinement
findings.why: `assertSafeLibraryId` is nothing but `SAFE_LIBRARY_ID_RE.test(id)` plus a throw, so both refinements build an exception just to discard it. The identical 8-line try/catch/return-true/return-false block appears twice in one file, and the caught error's message is thrown away in favour of a hardcoded duplicate.

findings.note: assertSafeLibraryId is only SAFE_LIBRARY_ID_RE.test plus a throw, and docs-libraries-config.ts wraps it in the identical throw-away try/catch twice (lines 34-43 and 50-59) purely to obtain a boolean — exception-as-control-flow duplicated in one file, though purely a readability cost.

findings.title: Two `directoryHasFiles` functions with identical semantics in the same directory, one hand-rolling a tree walk
findings.why: `docs-sync/cache.ts:7` already implements the same predicate in two lines on top of `collectAllFiles`. The 15-line stack-based copy here answers the same question a different way, so a reader comparing the sync-skip path with the validation path can't tell whether the difference is deliberate.
findings.fix: Delete the local implementation and import the `cache.ts` version (or move the two-line `collectAllFiles(dirPath).length > 0` helper into `libs/registry/src/utils/fs.ts` and use it from both).
findings.note: Verified both files: docs-sync/cache.ts:7 answers the question in two lines via collectAllFiles while output-validation.ts:28 hand-rolls a 15-line stack walk for identical semantics (the only difference is an early return), in the same directory.

findings.title: `readTsConfig` is used to parse `package.json`
findings.why: The function is a generic JSONC reader (comments + trailing commas stripped), but its name asserts a file kind. Reading `readTsConfig(packageJsonPath)` inside `resolvePackageConfig` looks like a bug at a glance and costs a detour to confirm it is not.

const packageJson = readTsConfig(packageJsonPath);
        if (packageJson.exports !== undefined) return null;
findings.fix: Rename `readTsConfig` to `readJsonc` (it already returns `Record<string, unknown>` and throws on a non-object), updating its four call sites in this file.

findings.title: `deleteRemovalFiles` re-passes `options.cwd` as a separate argument and restates `DeleteResult` inline
findings.why: The caller destructures `cwd` from `options` and then hands both to this three-line wrapper, so the same value arrives twice and can drift. The declared return type also duplicates the `DeleteResult` interface defined 170 lines above instead of referencing it.

findings.title: React useId string is reverse-engineered with regexes and radix 32 with no explanation
findings.why: This is the load-bearing mechanism for implicit scope resolution (it decides which scope owns an unscoped hotkey), and it decodes an undocumented React internal string format. findings.title: useFocusZone keeps both a validated and an unvalidated current zone and uses them inconsistently

findings.note: Verified: state.ts returns both `currentZone` and `safeZone`; use-focus-zone.ts feeds raw `currentZone` to the keyboard module while reporting `safeZone` publicly, and `setZoneValue` compares against the raw value, so with an out-of-`zones` current zone `transitions()` sees a zone the consumer was never told is active and `setZone(reportedZone)` fires onLeaveZone(invalid)/onEnterZone/onZoneChange — downgraded from high because every in-repo consumer passes a static `zones` constant, so it is currently only reachable via the type-cast edge-case test.

findings.title: Disabled flags are encoded as a "0101" string with nothing explaining why

findings.title: Length-prefixed registration key encoding is unexplained
findings.why: `${key.length}:${key}` joined with `|` is an injection-safe encoding chosen because hotkey strings may themselves contain `|` (it is an alias for `pipe`), so a naive join could make two different key sets produce the same version string and skip a re-registration. Without a note it looks like an arbitrary hash attempt.

findings.title: HastNode union is shaped so TypeScript cannot narrow it, forcing four `as` casts

findings.title: Clipboard availability pre-check bypasses the hook's own failure path

findings.title: Effect used only to relay a state change to a consumer callback

This effect exists purely to call `onStatusChange` after `imageStatus` changes — a notification the context setter could make directly, which also removes the `useEffectEvent` indirection and the `"idle"` skip condition that currently has to be re-derived.

The extra hop buys nothing and hides the registration effects from the component that owns them.

findings.title: `encodeIdPart` is a pure forwarding wrapper around `encodeURIComponent`, and a third id-encoding scheme
findings.why: The function body is a single call with the same argument — no transformation, no added logic. Worse, the library already has two id encoders for exactly this job (`lib/dom-id.ts` `encodeDomIdSegment`, used by Select and CommandPalette, and `hooks/listbox-dom.ts` `getEncodedListboxItemId`, used by Menu and NavigationList), so a reader has to decide which of three schemes applies where.

findings.title: `Omit<VariantProps<typeof statusIndicatorDotVariants>, "status" | "pulse">` resolves to `{}`

findings.title: `(number & {})` in a public type is the string-literal-widening idiom applied where nothing can widen
findings.why: `X & {}` exists to stop TypeScript absorbing literal members into a wider primitive, as in `"a" | "b" | (string & {})`. Here the wide member is `number` and no numeric literals are in the union, so nothing can be absorbed and `& {}` reduces to `number` exactly. It reads as a deliberate signal in a public exported type, and a reader must reason through variance rules to conclude it means nothing.

findings.fix: Write `export type ActiveHeadingActivation = "top-line" | "viewport-center" | number;` and regenerate the `active-heading` public registry JSON.
findings.note: Confirmed at use-active-heading.ts:6 — the `X & {}` idiom only prevents literal absorption into the same primitive, and this union's literals are strings while the wide member is `number`, so nothing can widen and `& {}` is inert noise in an exported public type; severity lowered to low since it is purely cosmetic (the resolved type and consumer autocomplete are identical either way).

findings.title: Base result exposes raw setHasStarted/setHasStreamed setters instead of a reset() operation

findings.title: The entire /api/git feature has no first-party consumer
findings.why: Nothing in libs/core/src/api (the shared client both surfaces use), apps/web, or cli/diffgazer ever calls /api/git/status or /api/git/diff — the review pipeline does its git work server-side via resolveGitDiff. AGENTS.md says cli/server is CLI-internal and 'consumed only by the diffgazer CLI', yet this feature ships a router, a service with realpath/symlink traversal defenses, and an undocumented `?path=` sub-directory capability (read via raw c.req.query in /status, bypassing the zod schema that declares it) that no caller and no doc mentions. It is exercised only by its own tests and listed in apps/docs api.mdx.
findings.evidence:
const relativePath = c.req.query("path");
const result = await resolveGitService({ basePath: projectRoot, relativePath });

findings.title: Manifest types and the integration-mode union are hand-restated instead of derived

findings.fix: Drop `.passthrough()` and validate with ReviewListQuerySchema directly (or add projectPath to the schema and read it from c.req.valid("query") if the intent was typed access).

findings.title: Writer and gate for the no-.js-imports contract use different matchers with different semantics
findings.why: stripRelativeJsExtensions (the writer) uses the lexical scanner and deliberately leaves comments/strings byte-identical, but the gate (libs/keys assertNoRelativeJsImports) re-checks the written output with RELATIVE_JS_IMPORT_RE, which matches inside comments and doc examples. A keys source doc comment containing `from "./use-navigation.js"` passes the writer, then hard-fails the build with 'Strip .js from libs/keys/src source imports' — an error the writer can never fix. The RE's own doc claiming it is 'the union of every form the registry writers ... must catch' is stale: no writer uses it.
findings.evidence:
export const RELATIVE_JS_IMPORT_RE =
  /((?:\bfrom\s+|\bimport\s*\(\s*|\brequire\s*\(\s*|\bimport\s+(?=["']))(["']))(\.{1,2}\/[^"']+)\.js\2/g;
findings.fix: Make the gate use the same lexical scanner (export a `findRelativeJsImportSpecifiers(content)` built on extractImportSpecifierRanges and have assertNoRelativeJsImports consume it), keep the regex only if some consumer truly needs comment-inclusive matching, and correct the doc comment.
findings.note: The divergence is real — stripRelativeJsExtensions uses the lexical scanner and leaves comments untouched while assertNoRelativeJsImports (libs/keys/scripts/transform-public-registry-imports.ts:98) and the other gates re-scan with the comment-blind regex — and the RE's docstring claim that it is what "the registry writers" must catch is provably stale since no writer uses it; the build-break scenario is hypothetical and human-fixable by editing the comment, so low rather than an architectural blocker.

findings.title: Wizard-abandonment cleanup effect is duplicated verbatim in web and TUI instead of living in core's useWizardState

findings.title: useSettingsFormFooter's canSave option is a third guard on a condition already enforced twice

findings.title: getListWindow's two-pass fixed-point loop for indicator-row reservation is unexplained
findings.why: The `attempt < 2` loop re-derives visibleRows after subtracting scroll-indicator rows, relying on the non-obvious invariant that indicator visibility is monotone under shrinking windows so two passes reach a fixed point; nothing in the file states why two iterations suffice or what the loop is converging on, failing the 30-second cold-reader test the confirmed ScrollArea/lifecycleVersion findings set the bar for.

findings.fix: Add a one-sentence constraint comment: reserving an indicator row can only turn indicators on, never off, so the reservation count is monotone and a second pass is guaranteed to be the fixed point.

findings.title: The only test covering the global 'q' Quit shortcut passes while the handler under test throws mid-execution

findings.title: Copy-mode installed source references bare `process.env`, so a stock Vite+React+TS app fails `pnpm build` right after `dgadd add`

Add an e2e assertion in cli/add/testing/e2e that copied output type-checks under `types: ["vite/client"]`, or the regression returns silently (libs/ui's own tsconfig has node types, so CI stays green).

findings.title: The relative-.js writer and the validation gate use different matchers with different semantics, and the docstring claims otherwise
findings.why: `stripRelativeJsExtensions` (the writer) rewrites only executable import specifiers via the lexer, while `RELATIVE_JS_IMPORT_RE` (used by all three gates) is a raw-text regex. The two disagree in both directions, so the gate can fail on content the writer refuses to touch (unfixable red build) and can pass content the writer would have rewritten (broken specifier ships). The JSDoc asserting it is "the union of every form the registry writers and the validate-artifacts gate must catch" is false — no writer uses it.

export const RELATIVE_JS_IMPORT_RE =
